issues.legal_issue: A civil suit may be brought to challenge as fraudulent a compromise decree made by a revenue forum of limited jurisdiction, notwithstanding the bar on separate suits to set aside compromise decrees.
material_facts: The suit sought to have a compromise decree made in proceedings before a revenue authority declared void, inoperative and not binding.

The plaintiff alleged that the compromise bore his father’s forged signature, that his father had received no notice or appeared in the proceedings, and that his father had died before the decree was made.
The decree arose from proceedings under a special land-reform statute, whose jurisdictional scheme assigned the matter to specified revenue forums.
The statute applied the Code of Civil Procedure to its proceedings, but the designated revenue authorities remained forums of limited and restricted jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: Order XXIII Rule 3-A did not bar the civil suit challenging the revenue forum’s decree. The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s order was set aside, and the suit was restored for trial; the ruling determined maintainability, not whether the fraud allegations were true.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXIII Rule 3-A ordinarily bars a separate suit to set aside a decree on the ground that its compromise was unlawful. Under Banwari Lal v. Chando Devi, (1993) 1 SCC 581, fraud may make a compromise unlawful, and the court that recorded the compromise is to decide its lawfulness under Order XXIII Rule 3, read with its proviso and explanation. But that bar does not prevent a civil suit concerning a decree or order made in proceedings before a forum of limited and restricted jurisdiction under another statute. Section 9 CPC gives civil courts jurisdiction over civil disputes unless expressly or by necessary implication excluded. Sections 331 and 341 and Schedule II of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act governed the revenue forum and the application of civil procedure; applying that procedure did not turn the revenue authority into a court under the Code. Revenue forums were not equipped or competent to effectively adjudicate fraud allegations with overtones of criminality.

rule.if: challenge_to_compromise_decree and proceeding_under_special_statute and decree_made_by_limited_revenue_forum and fraud_allegation_with_criminal_overtones and revenue_forum_lacks_effective_fraud_adjudication_capacity

predicates.challenge_to_compromise_decree: The claimant brought a suit seeking to challenge a decree based on a compromise.
predicates.proceeding_under_special_statute: The decree was made in a proceeding governed by a special statute.
predicates.decree_made_by_limited_revenue_forum: A revenue authority with limited and restricted jurisdiction made the decree.
predicates.fraud_allegation_with_criminal_overtones: The claimant alleged fraud in obtaining the compromise, involving circumstances with overtones of criminality.
predicates.revenue_forum_lacks_effective_fraud_adju: The revenue forum was not equipped or competent to effectively adjudicate the fraud allegations.

issues.definition: When a suit challenges a compromise decree from a special-statute proceeding before a limited revenue forum on fraud allegations that the forum cannot effectively adjudicate, the suit may proceed in civil court.
